The Signature

One deg. One recipe.
Every single morning.

The nihari at Waris is cooked low and slow overnight, so by sunrise the beef falls apart at the touch of a spoon and the gravy carries the deep, rounded heat Lahoris cross the city for. It is served the classic way — in a steel bowl, shining with rogan, finished at the counter in front of you.

Julienned gingerCut fresh every morning
Green chilliesSliced over the bowl, to taste
Lemon wedgesA squeeze to lift the gravy
Fresh corianderScattered on top, always

The Menu

What the morning offers

A short menu, done properly for over sixty years. When the deg is empty, the day is done — usually well before closing time on weekends.

House Special

Beef Nihari

The bowl Waris is famous for — slow-cooked beef shank in a thick, spiced gravy, finished with ginger, chillies, coriander and lemon.

Most Ordered

Special Nihari

The full works — a generous beef portion with the complete garnish spread and fresh bread from the tandoor.

For the Purists

Maghaz Nihari

Nihari topped with tender maghaz (brain), the old-school Lahori upgrade — rich, soft and deeply savoury. Arrive early; it finishes fast.

Limited Daily

Nalli Nihari

Served with bone marrow (nalli) melting into the gravy. Only a few portions come out of each deg, so regulars order it first.

From the Tandoor

Kulcha

Soft, blistered kulcha baked fresh through the morning — made for tearing and scooping up the last of the gravy.

From the Tandoor

Roghni Naan

Sesame-topped roghni naan with a gentle richness that stands up to the heat of the nihari.

On the Side

Garnish Plate

Extra ginger, green chillies, coriander, lemon and fried onions — build every bite exactly the way you like it.

Morning Classic

Lassi

A tall glass of traditional lassi — the cooling counterweight to a hot, spiced breakfast, just as it has always been served in old Lahore.

To Finish

Doodh Patti Chai

Slow-brewed milk tea to close the meal — the way a Lahori breakfast morning is supposed to end.

Portions and rates follow the day's market — call 0321 7373222 for today's availability, parcel orders and family packs.

The Morning Ritual

How a Waris breakfast works

01

Come early

Doors open at 6:00 AM and the deg is at its best in the first hours. On weekends, favourites like maghaz and nalli can sell out long before 1:30 PM.

02

Order your bowl

Plain beef, special, maghaz or nalli — your nihari is ladled to order and garnished at the counter with ginger, chillies, coriander and lemon.

03

Tear, scoop, repeat

Fresh kulcha or roghni naan, a squeeze of lemon over the gravy, and nowhere else to be. That is the whole ritual — unchanged since 1960.

Our Story

An Urdu Bazar landmark since 1960

Waris Nihari House stands at 7 Abkari Road in Urdu Bazar, in the heart of Anarkali — Lahore's oldest food streets. The signboard says it plainly: established 1960. Generations have started their day here, and many of today's customers were first brought by their fathers and grandfathers.

Nothing about the formula has needed to change: one dish, cooked overnight, served only in the morning, and finished when it's finished. That focus is why a small shop in the old city holds thousands of Google reviews — and why Lahoris still set their alarms for it.
